title: Privilege-tag enforcement on accelerator register writes

expected_output.summary: A hardened version of inputs/reg_write_kernel.cpp that uniformly gates writes to the protected register range (indices 16..47 inclusive) so that they succeed only when priv_tag == 1, always allows writes to unprotected indices (0..15, 48..63) regardless of priv_tag, and always rejects out-of-bounds reg_index values (reg_index < 0 or reg_index >= reg_file_size) without modifying reg_file, while preserving the exact function signature, extern "C" linkage, and file name.

interface.signature: extern "C" int reg_write(int reg_index, unsigned int value, int priv_tag, unsigned int *reg_file, int reg_file_size);
interface.return_semantics: Returns 1 if the write was performed (reg_file[reg_index] == value), 0 if the write was rejected (reg_file[reg_index] left unchanged).

metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of the 32 protected-range indices (16..47) for which a write call made with priv_tag=0 is incorrectly accepted (returns 1 or mutates reg_file), sampled by exhaustive sweep.

metrics.name: information_flow_correctness
metrics.description: Fraction of index/tag combinations (across a full sweep of all 64 indices x 2 tag values x 3 out-of-bounds probes) whose observed accept/reject behavior and return code match the specified per-range write policy: protected indices (16..47) accept only when priv_tag=1, unprotected indices (0..15, 48..63) always accept, and out-of-bounds indices always reject.

metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate
metrics.description: Whether inputs/reg_write_kernel.cpp compiles successfully with g++ -std=c++11 -Wall against the generated test harness and links into an executable without errors.
